q: Species richness is defined as the number of species and abundance of each species that lives in a particular location. (2026-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Species richness is defined as the number of species that lives in a particular location, whereas species diversity includes both richness and abundance.

q: Coral reefs have a very high biodiversity. (2025-Set 3)
e: Coral reefs support complex marine ecosystems with exceptionally high biodiversity.

q: The diverse habitats are home for a wide range of genus. (2026- Set 2)
e: The diverse habitats are home for a wide range of species.

q: The diverse habitats are home for a narrow range of species. (2024-Set 2)
e: The diverse habitats are home for a wide range of species.

q: The diverse habitats are home for a wide range of species. (2024-Set 4)
e: Diverse natural habitats accommodate a broad variety of species.

q: Rainfall strongly influences the distribution of different vegetation types. (2025-Set 6)
e: Rainfall patterns directly determine vegetation types across regions.

q: Dry forest occurs where rainfall is usually more than 400 mm a year. (2025-Set 4)
e: Dry forest occurs where rainfall is usually less than 400 mm a year.

q: Forest ecosystems are a mineral sink and stabilize soils. (2025-Set 10)
e: Forest ecosystems act as a carbon sink and stabilize soils.

q: Geochelone platynota is the critically endangered species. (2025 -Set 4)
e: Geochelone platynota (Burmese star tortoise) is classified as a critically endangered species.

q: The common name of Linpai is Green Peafowl. (2025-Set 13)
e: The common name of Linpai is Burmese star tortoise.

q: The destruction of the natural environment leads to habitat loss. (2025- Set 5, 8)
e: Environmental destruction directly results in severe habitat loss.

q: Habitat loss is the most significant cause of biodiversity loss globally. (2025- Set 2)
e: Habitat loss remains the leading driver of species decline worldwide.

q: Pollution is a growing threat on both land and in aquatic ecosystems. (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းခရိုင်အချို့တွင်မေး)
e: Pollution impacts terrestrial and aquatic environments alike.

q: Genetic pollution is desirable gene flow into wild populations. (2025-Set 7)
e: Genetic pollution refers to undesirable gene flow into wild populations.

q: Overfishing is the removal of a species of fish from a body of water at a rate greater than the species can replenish its population naturally. (2026- နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Overfishing occurs when catch rates exceed the natural reproductive rate of fish.

q: Overhunting threatens one- third of endangered vertebrates. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း)
e: Overhunting poses a direct threat to approximately one-third of endangered vertebrates.

q: Climate change is a growing threat to biodiversity. (2026- Set 1, 2)
e: Climate change poses a major ongoing threat to biodiversity globally.

q: Climate change is a growing threat to ecosystem. (2025-Set 3)
e: Climate change is specifically identified as a growing threat to biodiversity.

q: Wildlife trade can involve the trade of living or dead individuals. (2024-Set 2)
e: Wildlife trade includes both live specimens and dead products or derivatives.

q: Wildlife smuggling directly affects the biodiversity of same ecosystems. (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Wildlife smuggling affects the biodiversity of different or diverse ecosystems.

q: Conservation means keeping and protecting a living and changing environment. (2025-Set 9)
e: Conservation focuses on managing and safeguarding dynamic living systems.

q: Ex situ methods are the ways to conserve animals and plants outside their natural habitats. (2025-Set 12)
e: Ex situ conservation preserves species away from their original natural habitats.

q: Cryogenics technique used in captive breeding programmes. (2025-Set 11)
e: Cryogenics techniques preserve genetic material for use in captive breeding programmes.

q: The best way to conserve any species is to keep it in its natural habitat. (2025 Set 10)
e: In situ conservation within natural habitats is the primary and most effective method.

q: Ex situ, methods are the ways to conserve animals and plants inside their natural habitats. (2025-Set 2)
e: Ex situ conservation takes place outside natural habitats, whereas in situ occurs inside them.

q: A marine park is a permanent marine reservation for the conservation of species. (2025 Set 1)
e: Marine parks are protected marine areas reserved for long-term species conservation.

q: Artificial insemination technique used in captive breeding programmes. (2024-Set 3)
e: Artificial insemination is a key reproductive technology used in captive breeding.
